stem:
Omar looks at the diagram of a rectangular grid that is $3$ squares tall and $8$ squares wide. He wants the even-or-odd parity of the total number of small squares without multiplying $3 \times 8$.

Which claim correctly decides that parity?

teacher.key_rationale: The number of small squares is odd only when both dimensions are odd. Here 8 is even, so the total is even without multiplying. Naming the tall count, treating one odd side as enough for an odd total, or reversing cause and effect all miss that rule.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source polygon-on-grid as a labelled 3-by-8 rectangular grid.
